contradicted.reason: In Regular functions on a normal variety are cut out in codimension one, the objects are nonempty (empty varieties or empty affine charts are excluded by the register), so the empty case does not arise; the argument quantifies only over nonempty affine opens and their fibres.

upheld.reason: The hypothesis is braid isotopy; the conclusion is equivalence of the resulting oriented closures. Steps 1.1 and 2.1 construct the ambient isotopy. The words are equivalent occur in the consequent, not between the hypothesis and its converse.

Closure equivalence is not asserted to imply based braid isotopy here. Step 3.1 asserts only that closure factors through braid isotopy classes; its proof does not need the distinct converse classified by Markov moves.

The antecedent is a Markov move or finite Markov sequence; the consequent says its oriented closures are equivalent. Steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 realize the moves ambiently. Equivalence is the output relation, not an iff connective.

The Statement does not assert that every ambient isotopy of closures is a single Markov move or even give the converse finite-sequence construction. That separate converse is the later factorization and Markov theorem; this proof preserves closures only.

The detector keys on the definitional sentence 'has content $t$ exactly when it lies on the diagonal $c-r=t$', which is the defining equation $c(r,c):=c-r$ restated. The item is a Definition and asserts no conditional equivalence, so there is no forward direction to discharge; the not_applicable disposition stands.

The same definitional sentence is the only biconditional in the Definition, and it has no reverse direction to prove: reading 'content $t$' back from the equation $c-r=t$ is again the defining formula $c(r,c):=c-r$. The not_applicable disposition is therefore correct.

Every indexed aggregate in the claim is nonempty: $m$ runs over $1\le m\le n$, the paths of length $m$ ending at $\mu\vdash m$ exist for every $m\ge1$, and the partition sums run over $\lambda\vdash m$ with $m\ge1$. There is no empty level or empty index set, so no empty case arises.
